column3: Raises the reputations of an award winner: for a player, the world, home and current reputations rise by a fraction of the award's reputations (up to 10000 and at least them); for a non-player, they rise up to the award floors and the board confidence gains 1000. \n `award_raise_winner_reputation(person, club, national_rep, world_rep, for_player)`, called for the player-of-the-month slot (0x7671c0) and for the yearly and national side awards. A player (+0x61) in a player award: world (+0xd) + 5% of the award's world reputation, up to 10000 and at least that value; home (+9): for the club of his own nation (+0x53 = +0x1a of the person), + 10% of the national reputation and at least that value; otherwise + 2.5% of the sum and at least the average; current (+0xb) + 10% of the national reputation, at least that value; puts the player in the clubs' lists (0x842c00, with 1) if the list manager exists. A non-player (+0x69) in a non-player award: the three rise to the floors (+0xc world, +8 by the club's nation, +0xa national) and, with a club, the board confidence (+6 of the 73-byte row) + 1000, between 6500 and 10000. Only the low words of the reputations count.

Sends the prize money news to the club's human manager, only when the prize is at least 50 × the club reputation: the competition, the amount, the position, the round, the kind and, with the fixture, the opponent and whether the club won. \n `Comp::send_prize_money_news(club, amount (i64), position, round, fixture, kind)`, ret 0x1c; SEH frame only for the local news item. To the club's human manager (0x7875e0), with an amount of at least 50 × the reputation (+0x80), news 0x1a (0x77bbe0): 0 the competition (`[this+4]`), 1 the amount, 2 the club, 3 the position, 4 the round, 7 the kind; with the fixture, 5 the opponent and 6 whether the club won (+0x3d/+0x3e the penalty shoot-out winner [inference], otherwise +0x4b/+0x4c, otherwise +0x43/+0x44 the score); without it, −1 and 0. Delivered to him (0x7861e0).

Sends the TV rights news to the club's human manager: the club, the competition, the amount and the year. \n `Comp::send_tv_rights_news(club, amount)`, ret 8; SEH frame only for the local news item. To the club's human manager (0x7875e0), news 0x1f (0x77bbe0): 0 the club, 1 the competition (`[this+4]`), 2 the amount, 3 the competition year (+0x40), delivered to him (0x7861e0).

In the top competition, tells whether it and every competition down the chain are complete. \n Ret 0, method +0xc of the competitions: `Comp::all_stages_complete()`: only in the top competition (+0x1c ≤ −1), it and each one in the chain below (+0x20, the index into `[0xadadfc]`) must be complete (method +0x10 with 1, 1: push 1; push 1; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 8); returns 1 or 0 (in al).

Builds the vector of the distinct clubs of all stages (up to 200) and returns the count. \n Ret 8, method +0x58 of the competitions: `Comp::collect_club_list(&list, _)`: a vector of 200 pointers (0x944e46(0x320); out of memory: the box at line 0x681, a null list and 0) with the distinct clubs of all stages (−1 the competition itself up to +0x30; the others in `[+0xc]`): in a league (+0x43 = 2) those of table +0xb1 (rows of 0x3b bytes), otherwise those of +0xa7 (6 bytes), skipping null and repeated ones, up to 200; stores the vector in `list` and returns the count (word, in ax).

Finds the stage id, the status and the round the club reached, searching from the last stage back. \n Ret 0x10: `Comp::find_club_progress(club, &stage, &round, &status)`: over the stages from the last (+0x30) to the first (−1 the competition itself; the others in `[+0xc]`), skipping those with id 0x3fc: in a league (+0x43 = 2), the club's table row (0x6826d0 push i; mov ecx, stage -> thiscall, ret 4): stage = the id (+0x3a) and status = +0x37 of the row, and returns; in a cup, the last team of table +0xa7 (6 bytes) that is the club gives stage = the id and status = +5, and the round is the first round (from +0xab − 1 backwards, +0xa3 with 0x68 bytes, the ties of +0xad with 0x35 bytes) with a tie in which the team plays (+0 or +2): round = +7 of the round, and returns.

From the given stage backwards, returns the index of the first stage of the same group. \n Ret 4: `Comp::get_first_stage_of_group(k)`, used by the competition screens (0x4947a0): from stage `k` backwards, while the stages have the same group (0x4b01d0 of the id +0x3a: push id; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) and the index is greater than −1, the index of the first of them (k itself when it has no group).

Returns the first stage not finished (for a cup not yet started, the start of its group); with all finished, the start of the last one's group. \n Ret 0: `Comp::get_current_stage()`, used by the competition screens (0x48f8e0): the first stage (−1 the competition itself, up to +0x30) that has not finished (method 0x10 with (0, 1) = 0); if it is a cup (+0x43 = 1) that has not started (+0xab = 0), goes back to the start of its group through the previous stage (0x4b01d0 and 0x48d200: push k; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 4). All finished: the start of the last one's group. Invalid stage at the end: the box at line 0x36e and the competition itself; null stage: the competition itself.

Returns the active key of the key nation that owns the fixture: by the competition's nation, by the nations of the clubs in a friendly, 0 for the World Cup, 1 for national side tournaments. \n `comp_active_key_nation_of_fixture(competition, fixture)`, the key of the FIXTURE_MANAGER match lists (add_fixture 0x5aa680, find_fixtures 0x5acbe0, ...), of the quick simulation (0x6b66a0) and of the FIFA ranking weight (0x58cf70). Friendly (0x5c6710 over `[0xae2c74]`) or reserves (`[0x9cf684]`) with the given fixture and its competition being the friendly one (`[0xae2c74]`+4) or the reserves one: with either side a national side (0x53b900 of the clubs +0x1c/+0x20), 1; different nations (+0x53) or outside the selection (+0x11c), 3; the nation in the table of the 35 key nations (0xb63d60, 72 bytes each, selected in +0x11c), byte +0x14 of the row; otherwise 0 with the home side a national side and 3 without. Otherwise, a nation's competition (+0x5d): byte +0x14 of its row, or 3. Without a nation: World Cup and qualifiers (0x669a10), 0; international tournament (0x669ae0), 1; otherwise the key nation index (0x669470). TapeCall on every fixture searched: no counter.

Tells whether a round's fixtures are known: the stage is a league, or the round is before the current one, or it is the current last round with code 0x8c. \n Ret 8: `Comp::are_round_fixtures_known(stage, round)`: the stage (−1 = the competition itself; above +0x30: 0; below −1: the box at line 0x36e, as in the original) is a league (+0x43 = 2): 1. Otherwise 1 if the round is before the current one (+0xab, byte) or is the current one, the last (+0x3c − 1) and with code 0x8c (+7 of its 0x68-byte record in +0xa3); otherwise 0.

Returns 1 when the match round (+0x30) ends in 0 or is 1000 or above, else 0. \n Ret 8: `Comp::counts_for_fixture_clash(match, other)` (virtual +0x60 of the competitions, used by the date clash check 0x5adba0): 1 if the units digit (0x4b0850) of the round (+0x30, signed) is 0 (a round of 1000 or more also gives 0), otherwise 0. `other` is not read.

Daily update of the FA Cup. Rule: the FA Cup gathers its entrants on 3 October each year (Date(3, 9): month 9 is October; the community map says September), rebuilds the rounds and the tree and draws the preliminary round, once per season (+0x45); on 1 October 1999 it asked the human manager whether the club enters at the 5th round (+0xb2 marks the question); then, every day, the cup update. \n Ret 8; virtual +0x14 of the English cup; SEH frame for the news of the 1999 path, no destructor on the normal path: `EngFaCup::update_for_date(today, stage)`. With +0x45 = 0 and the stage different from 0: on Date(1, 9, 1999) (month 9 is October) with +0xb2 = 0, the question to the human manager about entering at the 5th round (only in 1999: the original routine through the trampoline); on Date(3, 9, today's year) (3 October), frees the tables, +0x45 = 1, the entrants (0x56fab0, thiscall), the rounds (virtual +0x8c), the tree (virtual +0x94) (a negative return gives the box, lines 0x3d6, 0x3dd, 0x3e4, and 1), the predicted order (virtual +0x5c) and the draw of the 1st round (0x51c800: push 0; mov ecx, cup -> thiscall, ret 4). Always, at the end, the cup update.

Daily update of the CONCACAF Champions' Cup. Rule: on the first day of the cup season (empty team table), picks the qualified clubs and the predicted positions; every day, the cup update (draws and matches). \n Ret 8; virtual +0x14 of the cup: `ConChamp::update_for_date(today, stage)`. With the team table empty (the club of team 0 = 0) and stage ≠ 0: the qualified clubs (0x4c11a0: mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0; negative: the box at line 0x1ba and returns 0) and the predicted positions (virtual +0x5c). Then the cup update (0x51f890: push stage; push today; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 8), whose return value is returned.

Sets up the rounds of the CONCACAF Champions' Cup. Rule: the cup prize fund is 2,000,000; the round table (three-round knockout) comes from virtual +0x3c. \n Ret 0; virtual +0x8c: `ConChamp::set_up_rounds()`; returns 1. The prize fund (+0x28) of 2,000,000 and the round table (+0xa3) from virtual +0x3c (push 0; push &+0x3a; push &+0x3c; push −1; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10).

Creates the round table of the CONCACAF Champions' Cup. Rule: 8 teams in single matches: quarter-finals drawn on 1/8 and played on 28/8, semi-final on 1/9 and final on 4/9; category 8, tie-break 3; no per-round prize (−1). \n Ret 0x10; virtual +0x3c: `ConChamp::create_round_table(stage, &rounds, &extra, &out)`: at stage −1, out (if requested) = 0, rounds = 3, extra = 0; the table (0x944e46 of 0x138; out of memory: the box at line 0x97 and 0) with the 3 rounds and, in the first two, day 0 of the empty tie (0x521f10 with −1, −1, −1 and home 0; the original calls it between the match and the fields, which do not overlap). Outside −1, 0.

Builds the table of the first group of the Copa Libertadores. Rule: group 1 has 4 clubs, the first 4 drawn, each in the row of its order; human managers get the group draw news. \n Ret 0: 4 teams (+0x3e), table +0xb1 (0x944e46(0xec): push 0xec; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; 4 rows of 0x3b bytes; out of memory: the box at line 0x16f and returns 0), each row i with drawn club i (+0xee) (0x687430 League::init_table_row: push 0; push 0; push club; push i; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10), the group draw news (0x684230: mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0) and returns 1. The same body as 0x4019c0 of the African Nations Cup (only the file and the box line change).

Creates a group stage of the Copa Libertadores. Rule: each of the other groups is a league stage with the next 4 drawn clubs (4g + 4 to 4g + 7), the cup's rules and year and the cup's round table for the group; human managers get the news. \n Ret 4; SEH frame only for the stage's new (no destructor on the normal path): the stage of group g + 1 (g from 0 to 6, from the draw day). The teams in a vector of +0x3e pointers (0x944e46(+0x3e << 2): push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; out of memory: the box at line 0x218 and 0): drawn clubs 4g + 4 to 4g + 7 (+0xee); the round table through virtual +0x3c (push 0; push &id; push &rounds; push g; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10); the stage (0x944cf1(0xee) push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; the League_Stage constructor 0x68b100, thiscall, ret 0x58, 22 arguments: the cup, the teams (+0x3e, word), the vector, +0x3c (word), +4, the round table, the rounds (word), +0xc2, +0xc3, +0xc4, &+0xc5, &+0xbe, the year +0x40 (word), g, the id (word), +0x51, 2, 0, +0xd9 (word), −1, 0, 2; the original pushes the words and bytes with garbage in the high bytes, which the constructor does not read: the copy passes clean values) in `[+0xc][g]`; the vector and the round table are freed (0x9452ca). No stage: the box at line 0x22e and 0. With it: the group news (0x684230 on the stage), +0x30 = g and 1.

Selects the clubs qualified for the Libertadores. Rule: takes the 32 clubs marked with it as the season's continental competition (the mark comes from league qualification), in database order, then shuffled (96 random swaps) for the groups; any other count is an error (the box). \n Ret 0: `ConmebolLiber::select_qualified_clubs()`: +0xf2 = 32 and the list +0xee (0x944e46(0x80): push 0x80; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; out of memory: the box at line 0x285 and returns 0) with the clubs, in database order, whose season competition (+0x1db) is the Libertadores, up to 32; fewer than 32: the box at line 0x297 and returns 0; otherwise the list is shuffled (0x4afb40(list, 32): push n; push list; add esp, 8 -> cdecl; 3 × 32 random swaps) and returns 1.

Counts the results in the national side's history between two months (year × 12 + month), from the end, for the work permit. \n Ret 0x14: `FIFA_RANKINGS::count_results_in_period(nation, month_from, year_from, month_to, year_to)` (used by the work permit 0x8c7950, with the two years up to today): in the nation's entry (id `[nation]`, 0x2c bytes in table `[this]`), the history (+4, 5-byte entries: points, month +2, year +3; count +0xa) from the end to the start; a year × 12 + month before the start of the period stops the search, up to the end of the period each one counts. In 16 bits. TapeCall on every permit that reaches the national side matches: no counter.

Updates the FIFA rankings on the 18th: drops the results older than a year, sorts the histories, rolls the yearly totals and redoes scores and positions. \n Ret 4: `FIFA_RANKINGS::update_rankings(date)` (from the national sides' day 0x76b100): only on the 18th (0x54cf70). Stores the date in +5 (0x417c10) and, in each nation (`[0xae2350]` entries), removes from the history the results older than a year (year + 1 before today's, or the same year with the month before today's, 0x54cfb0), putting the last one in its place; the loop goes from the low byte of the count − 1 down to 0, as in the original. Then sorts the history by points (qsort 0x945333 with 0x58e220). In the month stored in +4, with the year different from that of `[0xdd6ec8]`, the yearly totals move one slot (+0x14 → +0x28) and +0x14 is zeroed. Finally the scores (0x58dfc0) and the positions: the order (0x58d610) gives position + 1 in +0x10, with the previous one in +0x12; the order vector is freed (0x9452ca).

Appends the points, month and year of the match to the national side's history, growing the array by 5 entries when full. \n Ret 0xc; SEH only for the local date, with an empty destructor: `FIFA_RANKINGS::append_result(nation, points, fixture)` (from the international result 0x58cf70, for each national side): with the count (+0xa) equal to the capacity (+8), the capacity grows by 5 and the history (+4) is reallocated (0x945667) or allocated (0x944e46) with capacity × 5 bytes. The new entry, in the place of the old count: the points (16 bits), the match month (+2) and the year (+3).

Returns the national side's strength tier from 1 to 4, by reputation and ranking position. \n Ret 4: `FIFA_RANKINGS::get_nation_strength_tier(nation)` (twice per international result 0x58cf70): reputation (+0x8e) below 3000 and position (+0x10 of the entry) below 50: 3; reputation below 6000 and position below 15: 2; otherwise by position: below 21, 1; below 61, 2; below 101, 3; else 4.

Recalculates the scores: the year total from the best eight results and the score from the totals of this year and the five before. \n `FIFA_RANKINGS::recalculate_scores()` (from the update of the 18th 0x58d460): in each nation, the sum of the points of the first eight results (the history comes sorted) and that of all; with more than eight, the year total (+0x14) is (all × 8 / count + eight) / 2, otherwise the eight. If the date of `[0xdd6ec8]` is after today minus 365 days (0x54c8e0), with fewer than nine results the total is (+0x18 + eight) / (count + 8) × 8 (with no results, +0x18). The score (+0xc, f32): (+0x14 + 5/6 of +0x18 + 4/6 of +0x1c + 3/6 of +0x20 + 2/6 of +0x24 + 1/6 of +0x28, each part truncated) × `[0x96a350]`.

Returns a new array with the ranking entries of the nations that have a national side, sorted by score, and the count. \n Ret 4: `FIFA_RANKINGS::collect_ranked_order(&count)` (from the update of the 18th 0x58d460 and from the ranking screen): a vector (0x944e46) of `[0xae2350]` pointers; without it, the "Error" box (line 0x1e3) and 0, without storing the count. The table entries (0x2c bytes) of the nations with a national side (+0x71 of the nation, 0x122-byte records in `[0xae23a8]`), sorted by score (qsort 0x945333 with 0x58e240); the count goes in `count`.

Creates the initial FIFA ranking table. Rule: each nation's points are its database strength ÷ 35, repeated as the points of each of the 6 years [inference] (× 1000); the position comes from the points order. \n Ret 0, `FIFA_RANKINGS::create_default_table`: the initial FIFA ranking table (0x2c-byte records, one per nation, calloc 0x945501 of `[0xae2350]` × 0x2c in +0; out of memory: the box at line 0x2da). Each record: +0 the nation index; the nation's strength (+0xa8, double, 0x122-byte nations in `[0xae23a8]`) × 1/35 gives the points (+0xc, float) and, × 1000 (truncated, _ftol), the 6 dwords +0x14..+0x28 [inference: the points of each of the last years]. Then the order by points (0x58d610(this, &count), thiscall, the sorted list of the nations with a continent) gives the position: +0x12 = the previous position (+0x10) and +0x10 = 1, 2, 3...; the list is freed.

Builds the group A table of the African Nations Cup. Rule: group A has four national teams, the first four of the draw list, in order; the managers get the draw news. \n Ret 0: `AfricanNations::init_group_a_table()`: group A with 4 teams (+0x3e), table +0xb1 (0x944e46(0xec): push 0xec; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; 4 rows of 0x3b bytes; out of memory: the box at line 0x1f1 and returns 0), each row i with national side i of the draw list (+0xee) (0x687430: push 0; push 0; push national side; push i; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10), the group draw news (0x684230: mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0) and returns 1.

Sets the season expectations of each club in the table, through the manager manager, with the news. \n Ret 0, a league method: `League::set_club_season_expectations()`: with the manager manager (`[0xb67a44]`), the season expectations of each club in the table (+0xb1, rows of 0x3b bytes, +0x3e clubs) through 0x6a3770 (push 1; push club; mov ecx, `[0xb67a44]` -> thiscall, ret 8: with the news).

Moves the club down to the division (keeping the previous one), applies the relegation clauses and makes the human manager leave when the division is not played. \n Ret 0xc; this is not read: `League::relegate_club_to_division(club, division, _)`: the club's competition (+0x57) becomes the division and the previous one goes to +0x5b; the relegation clauses (0x4cd030 push old; push club; mov ecx, `[0xae1050]` -> thiscall, ret 8); if the division is not played (no competition table `[0xadadfc]`, no division or no competition with its id) and the club has a human manager who decides (0x600a50 push 0; push 0; push 1; push 1; push club; add esp, 0x14 -> cdecl), the manager leaves (0x69b790 push 0; push 7; push 1; push club; mov ecx, `[0xb67a44]` -> thiscall, ret 0x10).

Moves fixtures for TV: on the TV table dates, each slot takes the highest-rated fixture (a random draw by reputation, zeroed when either club plays 2..5 days before or after; 100/50 in national team slots) to the weekday and time slot of the slot, with the news, the stadium and the calendar. \n Ret 4; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path (the local dates and list): `League::move_fixtures_for_tv(date)`, from the league day (0x6847c0) and from building the calendar (0x683e30). Through the date's entry (tv_date_entry), the league matches on the entry's day and time slot (+4) go to a local list (0x68d020; 0x5abd90: push list; push league +0x44; push -1; push id; push slot; push day; push year; mov ecx, `[0xae2a58]` -> thiscall, ret 0x1c). With matches: the entry's slots (7 bytes from +5, up to the first with +0xb = 0xff) are sorted (0x945333 with 0x8b4e00) if any has bits 0x7fc0 in dword +5. For each slot with time slot (+0xa) 0..2: the date moved to the slot's weekday (+9; 0x54a2d0); the clash window: 2..5 days after the requested date if the TV day falls after it, otherwise 5..2 days before (0x54c5b0/0x54c8e0 + 0x417c10). Among the matches in the list (of the league's type, +0x42), the one with the highest rating (signed word; the first on a tie): slot of type 3, 100 for a national side match (0x53b900 on the home side) in the stadium (+0x18 → +0x38 → +0x1f) of the nation of either side, otherwise 50; otherwise the random draw (0x90cfc0) of the away side's reputation (+0x80) + 1500 plus that of the home side's, zeroed if either has a match in the window (0x5acbe0). The chosen one: outside type 3, news 3 to both clubs; it leaves the calendar (0x5abc30), takes the TV date, the time slot and the slot's type, the stadium (0x85c260) and goes back into the calendar (0x5aa680); the slot becomes 0xff and the match leaves the list (0x68d1f0).

Sends the group draw news 0x15 (the competition, the first date, the opponents) to each human-managed club in the group. \n Ret 0; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path: `League::send_group_draw_news()`, from the competitions' group draw. A group of up to 8 teams (+0x3e; the 0x3b-byte teams in `[+0xb1]`, +0 the club): for each club with a human manager, news 0x15 (allocated once, 0x944cf1(0xdf), built by 0x77bbe0, freed at the end by 0x944c94 without a destructor) with the competition id, +0x3a, the first date (that of the first entry of table `[+0xba]` moved to the weekday of each slot, 0x54a2d0, the earliest), the number of opponents; per club, its own id (2) and those of the others (6 onwards), delivered to it (0x7861e0).

Sends news 0xd with the first three fixtures (date, opponent, venue) to each human-managed club not yet told, and does the same in the following stages. \n Ret 4; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path (the local lists): `League::send_fixture_list_news(list)`, from creating the calendar (0x5cd1e0) and from the league day in its year. Uses the local list (0x68d020) if the league is a first stage (+0x44 = 0xff) or there is no list. With the competition counting (0x4b0700: push id; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) and a first stage: the date of the first entry of table `[+0xba]` minus 5 days (0x54c8e0, 0x417c10); for each club with a human manager (0x3b-byte teams in `[+0xb1]`) that is not in the list (4-byte ids): its first 3 matches from that date (0x5acee0 into a local list, 18 arguments: push 1; push -1; push +0x44; push 0; push list; push 3; push -1 ×4; push club id; push -1; push -1; push competition id; push 1; push &slot; push &day; push &year; mov ecx, `[0xae2a58]` -> thiscall, ret 0x48); finding 3: news 0xd (competition id, club id, the league year and, per match, the day, the year, the opponent and 1 at home or 0 away) to the club, which enters the list (0x68d0d0: push 4; push club; mov ecx, list -> thiscall, ret 8). Then, in the stages (`[+0xc]`, up to +0x30) with +0x43 = 2, the same routine with the list.

Creates the season fixtures: the round-robin grid (with the club order drawn) or the year's own list, home and away by the parity of the half and the year, the stadium, date and slot of each round, and the calendar; then the TV dates. \n Ret 0; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path (the local dates): `League::create_fixtures()`, from building the competitions (44 calls up to 2002-06-01). With n = teams (+0x3e) + teams % 2: +0xdd = 0; the grid of n rows of n dwords (0x944cf1; out of memory: the box at line 0x3fc or 0x405 and 0), built by 0x6844b0 (push n; push grid -> stdcall, ret 8: it does not read the mov ecx, this before it) and, outside competitions `[0x9cf79c]` and `[0x9cf7a4]`, the club order drawn (0x686a70: push n; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 4). The match record (0x4f bytes on the stack): +0 competition id, +8 = -1, +0x14 the competition, +0x24/+0x26 the last date of the table (+0xba, entry +0xa9 − 1), +0x2c year (+0x40), +0x30 = 0, +0x32 (+0x3a), +0x36 (+0xdb), +0x38 (+0xab), +0x3a (+0xc4), +0x3b = 0xff, +0x3d/+0x3e = 0, +0x42 stage (+0x44), +0x43..+0x4c = 0xff, and the league's method 0x7c with it. With its own list (+0xea, 0x10-byte entries: +8/+0xc the club ids) for the league year: in each round k (+0xa9) the teams/2 matches of the list (the indices through table +0xb1), and the list is freed (0x9462bb + 0x944c94). Otherwise the round robin: for j = 1..legs (+0x3c)·(n − 1), the round through 0x68a030 (push +0xd9; push +0xa9; push +0x3c; push +0x3e; push id; push &step; push round; add esp, 0x1c -> cdecl) and column j % (n − 1) (n − 1 at zero): each team i with opponent v ≠ 0 in the grid clears the opponent's slot; home advantage by the parity of v > 0, of the half ((j − 1)/(n − 1)) and of year + stage; with nation +0x24, the club of that nation (+0x69) stays at home. Each match goes to the calendar (add_league_fixture). At the end, the grid is freed and the type 3 dates of the table take the matches to TV (0x685640). Returns 1.

Chooses the match's standout player: 16-bit score (disposition + 125 × (0x10 + 2 × 0x0c) + 50 × 0x03 + 35 × 0x06) and ftol(disposition × factor); stores the record's id at 0x477a. \n The standout among the first (byte 0x4d of the fixture & 0xf) + 11 of each side (inactive ones, with 0x20 = 0xff, left out): score (16 bits) = disposition 0x35 + 125 × (0x10 + 2 × 0x0c) + 50 × 0x03 + 35 × 0x06; replaces only with a higher score and ftol(disposition × factor) not lower. Stores the first dword of the player sheet (0x69) at 0x477a.

The match engine loop: `n` match instants. Match already decided: quick simulation, standout, closing, humans' instructions restored, referee rating (2). Each instant: punishments, shoot-out, kick-off, drawn substitution, marked incident, restart and taker; on the clock, abandonment (8), period (4) and full time (2 or 4); then possession, each player's time, lines, nearest to the ball, marking and each active player's decision (0x7103e0), with the pending shot and the contest. Validated by the career. \n Ret 4: the engine loop, `n` instants of the match. Match already decided (+0): quick simulation (0x6beeb0), standout (0x6d0f80), closing, the humans' instructions restored and the referee rating (0x6d4a20); returns 2. Otherwise clears the player sheets and the pointers of those who left and, at each instant: pending punishments (0x6d1210), penalty shoot-out (0x6be710; at the end, 2), the narrated kick-off (0x212f/0x1f74), the randomly drawn substitution, the marked incident (0x6bac40/0x6bba10), the restart (0x6c54a0) and the set-piece taker (0x6ceb90). On the clock (+0x8ed0): end by abandonment (8), the period (0x6bd930: 4 at the breaks; end of the match with the aggregate score, 0x896290 and 2 or 4). Ball in play (0x6bbe40) or stopped adds stoppage time; otherwise possession (0x6cf750), each player's time (0x6f4aa0), the lines (0x6c3aa0, 0x6cd660, 0x6bd760), those nearest to the ball, the pressure in the areas (0x6bd6b0), the marking (0x7160f0/0x6bc030) and each active player's decision (0x7103e0), with the pending shot (0x6f6c00) and the contest (0x6c9cd0). Returns 1 at the end of the `n` instants.

Lines the teams up for a set piece of side +0x8eae: counter +0xf5c6 + 54 × side; releases the ball. Ball in the side's own area: formation (as 0x6c4ec0) and whoever of the other side lands on the spot moves one row. Otherwise: spot clamped to the grid, far (+0x8eb1 = 7) or near (−1), base column 4 − draw + draw, base row 3/4 from the spot; near, everyone from the set-piece table (12 rows × 9 columns per position and kicking side); far, by role (0x716270 in attack: 1 deep, 2 middle; 0x716310 in defence: 4 deep, 3 middle). Finally the taker (0x6ceb90, type +0x8eb2) goes to the spot, takes the ball and aims (0x6f4920). Cell off the grid: fatal error, as in the original. \n Details: counter +0xf5c6 + 54 × side goes up; +0x8eae = -1; the ball is released (0x6f0970). Ball in the side's own area (row < 3 on side 0, > 8 on side 1): each player goes to his formation cell (as 0x6c4ec0), and whoever of the other side lands on the ball's spot moves one row; on the kicking side, whoever passed the line goes back one (0x6f5b80). Otherwise (spot clamped to 0..=8 × 0..=11): far from goal (+0x8eb1 = 7) or near (-1); base column 4 - random(2) + random(2) and base row 3 (near) or 4 (far) from the spot towards the goal. Near: everyone from the side's set-piece table (+0xf56e, 12 rows per column, 9 columns per position and kicking side). Far: by role: in attack (0x716270) 1 goes deep and 2 to the middle, in defence (0x716310) 4 deep and 3 to the middle, the others from the table. Middle: x 4 ± random, row 6 (side 1) or 5. Deep: x of the base column ± random and row 0..1 or 10..11 next to the attacked or defended goal. Whoever passed the line goes back one (0x6f5b80). Cell off the grid: the original ends the game (fatal error). \n At the end the taker (0x6ceb90 with type +0x8eb2) goes to the spot, takes the ball (0x6f0630) and aims (0x6f4920, 4, 1 on side 1 or 10), with +0x19c = 200. Everyone zeroes +0x2b (0x7160e0).

The ordering of the day's matches (qsort): competition, record fields and the club name. \n The order of the day's matches (0x69-byte records): by competition (+4), then +0x46 (byte), +0x36, +0x38 and +0x34 (words) and, when everything ties, by the name of the first club (+0x20 → +0x38) with the text comparison 0x90c1d0 (case-insensitive).

The players' order on the engine's turn (qsort): the marked ones first, then by strength. \n The order of the players on the engine's turn (`[0xb67a64]`): with +0x8eb2 set, the one in +0xf582 comes first; then the one in +0x91de; the rest by strength (+0x104 + +0x105) × (+0x3b × 0.005 + 0.5) × +0x4d (f32), truncated, from highest to lowest.

Decides whether a context commentary (league race, club news) may play now. \n Ret 0xc: may context commentary `event` (0x21a3..=0x21af: the league race, the club's recent news) play now for `side`? Outside the range 8000..=0x21e4, already played (table at +0x21e per side) or without a competition (+0x4792 → +0x14): no. It weighs the aggregate score (0x6ce310), the club's row in the league table (0x4a4850: +0x19/+0x41 and +0x2d/+0x55), the minute (+0x8ed0 / 11), the club's news in the last 10 or 30 days (0x757da0 on the media `[0xb6b7c8]`) and the average of the side's 20 players (+0x47cb, step 0x1be, the marked ones at −0x1c); those in the table write the value into `out`. The events in the range outside the 13 cases: yes.

Reads back the events described in `desc` from the file with the right number. \n Ret 4: reads back the events described in `desc` (position, count, number, human) into +0x720 of record `e` (+6 = count): looks for the file with the number (version 1, otherwise error 0xbf6/0xc11, with the file left open as in the original). Returns whether it read them.

Reads `events_<language>.cfg` (or `events_eng.cfg`) into the table of the 677 event codes at `[0xb68788]` (7 option bytes, the 0x110-byte sounds with weight, type, name and the two texts `G`/`R`); checks `<X` tokens, events without text and, with `-verifysounds`, the sound files; at the end converts the weights and gives the default sound to those without one. \n About 5.2 KB: reads `events_<language>.cfg` (CM3_DATA; without it, `events_eng.cfg`, and without that the game stops, error 0xcc4) into the table of the 677 event codes at `[0xb68788]` (0x12 bytes: 7 option bytes, +8 the 0x110-byte sounds, +0xc count, +0xe the weight). With a different language since the last read, 0x6d5b50 clears first; already read (`[0xb6b723]`), nothing. Lines: `=id,o0..o6` opens an event (o4 between 0 and 11; o2 without o0 warns 0xd40), `>weight,type,name` adds a sound (with `-verifysounds` on the command line, checks the file in CM3_SOUNDS), `G`/`R` the two texts of the last sound (allocated; unknown `<X` tokens warn). At the end, the weights become (largest × 10) / weight and +0xe the sum; an event without a sound gets the default sound (0xb68670). Reads through the game's `fgetc` and uses buffer `[0xde1f64]`, as the original.

Builds the event sound's `R` text with the tokens replaced (`` player, ``/`` club, `` competition, `` stage, ``/`` number, ``/`` referee), `{...}` prefix and suffix (0x6701f0) and upper case; writes to `[0xb67ea0]`. \n Stdcall, ret 0x10: the text of event `ev` (+0 code, +2 which sound, +5/+6 and +7/+8 the two players (side, index), +9 a number) of match `ctx` (+0/+4 the clubs, +0x40 the referee), with `comp` the competition (-1 none) and `variant` the segment between `|` (0 the first). Reads the `R` text (+0x10c) of the chosen sound (at most the last) and replaces the tokens: ``/`

` player (0x6db2d0), ``/`` club, `` competition, `` its stage (0x4bfa30/0x4bff70), ``/`` the number (+1), `` the number in words (0x90c310), ``/`` the referee ("Mr ..." or "the referee" depending on the language and a remainder of division by 5), ``/`` nothing. `{...}` before or after the token are prefix and suffix (0x6701f0, which applies article and gender); a following letter `C` puts it in upper case (0x90c2d0). Writes into `[0xb67ea0]` (and returns it), recounting the length with `strlen` after each token, as the original; without an event, without text or without the requested segment, 0. An unknown token warns 0xb10.

The commentator writes the event on the panel and plays its sound: restores the crowd sound, builds the event's `G` text (like 0x6d8d10) into a line with the club colours (`<O>` the other's, `<Y>`/`<R>` the default ones), wraps or cuts with "..." by the width (0x5e5ad0, 0x90cb20), draws on the panel (0x801040…0x800580), plays the event sound (0x8025e0) and marks the time and duration (+0x2d6c, +0x2dac). \n Ret 0x20, about 4.4 KB: commentator `nar` writes event `ev` of match `ctx` on `panel` (0xb74450) and plays its sound. First, the crowd noise of the human whose turn it is (`[0xb77c7a]`; channel +0x20, "fxloop2.wav") is restored if it stopped. With a valid code and option 1 zeroed, builds the `G` text (+0x108) of the chosen sound (segment +0xd between `|`) as 0x6d8d10 does, but in its own line and with colours: it starts with those of the club in the incident (0x53b640 with the side's kit), `<O>` switches to the other's, `<Y>` and `<R>`/`<r>` without `f` the default ones (`[0xaebdea]`/`[0xaebdec]` or `[0xae31a8]`); `<N>` is the number, `<n>` in words; the player name is the short one if the whole text fits in less than 300 (0x5e5ad0 with the `font`). Too wide for `width` - 16: wraps (0x90cb20) or cuts at a word with "...". Draws (0x801040, 0x801660, 0x801960, 0x801c70, 0x800d30, 0x800580 with option 3). Finally, without a segment (+0xd) and with volume (+0x2db0 >= 101), plays the event sound (0x8025e0 on the channel from option 6, side from option 5), and marks the time and the sound duration (+0x2d6c, +0x2dac = weight × volume / 100).

Returns the next commentary event to show, part by part of the text (split by `|`), advancing the queue reading. \n Ret 4: the next commentary event to show (0 with the queue switched off, +5): skips the empty slots; in the event's text (table `[0xb68790 + 0x12 × (event − 8000)]`, 0x110-byte record +2, +0x108) moves to the next part separated by `|` (the current part in +0xd; bit 0x8000 marks that there is more) and, when the text is finished, advances the reading. In `out`, the slot's 0x86-byte record (+0xd8).

The player name in the commentary: the short form, or the long one when another player of either club has the same short name. \n Writes into `buf` (`size` bytes) the name of player `player` on side `side` of match `pt` (0x49-byte record at +0x190: id and the three names +0x198..+0x1a0, sides of 0x625 bytes) through 0x53e140: with `short` and random(5) = 0, form 1; otherwise form 5, and if any of the 100 players of either club (+0, +4; list from 0x541f90) with another id or another name has the same form 5, the `long` form.

Combines the new commentary event with the last queued one (returns the combined event and copies the previous player, side and value). \n Ret 8: combines the new event `e` (14 bytes: event word; +5, +6 player and side; +7, +8 the other; +9 integer) with the last one in the queue (position +8 − 1 in the ring of 12, 14-byte records at +0x30): returns the combined event (negative = replaces the previous one; 0 = no combination) and, in combinations, copies the player, the side, the other and the integer of the previous one into `e`. `m` is the engine (0 outside the match): it gives the side in possession (+0x8eab) and the ball in the area (0x6d58f0). The original's two calls to 0x6cb960 have no effect and their value is discarded (they are left out).

Puts an event at the front of the commentary queue (steps the 12-slot ring back, drops the repeat) and queues it via 0x6d6f70. \n Ret 0x1c: the write position (+8, ring of 12) steps back one slot (from 0 it goes to 11); if the last one in the queue (+6 items, word +0x712 of 14 bytes) is the same event as at the new position (+0x30), the queue loses one; then queues through 0x6d6f70 with the same 7 arguments.

The commentary queue constructor: clears the queue, reads the events and, if asked, plays the crowd loop. \n Ret 4: zeroes the queue and the fields (+0x2db0 = 125, +1 and +0xa = −1, +0x2d68 = −1), the event globals (0xb68670..), reads the events (0x6d9e50), marks the 16 slots (+0x10, +0x20) with −1 and zeroes the 16 times (+0x2d6c); with `crowd`, plays the crowd loop of the side whose turn it is (`[0xb77c7a]`) through 0x8025e0. Returns `this`.

Frees the loaded event tables and each record's texts. \n In each of the 0x12-byte entries from 0xb68790 to 0xb6b72a with its own table (neither null nor the default 0xb68670), the two texts (+0x108, +0x10c) of each 0x110-byte record and the table; then zeroes 0xb6b723 and puts −1 in 0xa1599c.

Tells whether the sounds of the 16 marked events have played and passed their window (clock 0x90c510; stops the finished channels, 0x802a50). \n Ret 4: have the sounds of the `active` events (16 marks) played? For each marked one, a channel (+0x10 + k; -1 free, -2 waiting) that is still playing (0x8029f0 on 0xb74450) holds; one that has finished is stopped (0x802a50) and freed. Returns 1 only if all marked ones have passed their window (+0x2d6c + 4k up to + `[+0x2dac]`, by clock 0x90c510).

Swaps the commentary event for a variant, by a random draw and by the play type. \n Stdcall, ret 0xc: with random(3) ≠ 0 it stays the same; otherwise, by the play type `type` (1, 2, 8, 0x10, 0x20, the last with another random(3)) there are swap tables; plays 2..4 (low byte of `sides`) have their own, and the upper byte 3..5 swaps 0x1f4b for 0x217e.

Sends the club international report news: the match squad is sorted by club; each group of the same club becomes news 0x24 to its manager: the match data, the star player, how many, up to 4 players (the star first, the others by how they did), random(2) and the codes; the group players leave the array. \n Ret 0x18; SEH frame for the local news item: `NationalTeams::send_club_international_report_news(club, match, result, star, squad, count)`, from the result between national sides (0x76b600), for each side. The squad (a vector of `count` persons, the low byte) is sorted by club (0x945333 with 0x778ef0); each group of players of the same club becomes news 0x24 to the club's manager (0x7861e0): the match record for the club (0x7e4750, only once) and its data (0x7e4de0), the star player (id and keys, if he is from the club; otherwise −1 in the four), how many there are, the club, up to 4 players (the star first, the others by the code of how they did, from highest to lowest), 0x420e9, random(2) and the codes. The group's players leave the vector (zeroed).

Posts the call-up news: the called-up players (flag 4, or 8 for the second team) of human-managed clubs, grouped by club, become news 0x1d to the manager: national side, club, type, how many, the opponents (given list or built by 0x76d560) and up to 3 players. \n Ret 0x1c; SEH frame for the local news item: `national_teams_post_call_up_news(national_side, second, match, type, no_opponents, opponents, count)`, from the call-up (0x76c120) and from the screen. Of the 50 slots of the national side's squad (+0xd7, pointers), each player with the flag (+0x5e: 8 for the second team, otherwise 4) and a club with a human manager (0x7875e0) joins his club's group; when the next one in the slot is not from the same club (or lacks the flag, or the list ended), news 0x1d goes to the club's manager (0x7861e0): the national side, the club, `no_opponents`, the type, how many, `second`, how many opponents and, with fewer than 4, their ids (from the given list or built once by 0x76d560 with the match, when there is no list and no `no_opponents`), and up to 3 players (id and keys). The list built here is destroyed and freed at the end (0x68d040, 0x944c94).

Returns a new list with the match opponent (its nation's first team, for the second team) and the opponents of the fixtures from tomorrow to 13 days later that are not finals. \n Ret 8; SEH frame for the local list: `national_teams_collect_fixture_opponents(national_side, match)`, from the call-up news (0x76e0b0) and from the request to the manager (0x76f1a0). A new list (0x944cf1 with 0xe, 0x68d020) with the match opponent (the away side if the home side is from the national side's nation, otherwise the home side; for the second team, the main national side of its nation, 0x53b4f0) and the opponents of the national side's other matches from tomorrow to 13 days later (0x5acbe0, with byte +0x40 of the match) that are not final-stage matches (the nine national side competitions). Returns the list.

The national squad selection (senior, B/Olympic or under-21): in the finals the list item; the squad dates, the ages and the size; with a human manager, the request to him; otherwise those from another side and the flagged ones leave, the pool list goes to the slot assignment and each picked player who fits the slot joins the squad (leaving the previous side and the tactic slots); the sorting, the news and the tactic slots. Approved fix of the original (01/11/2026): position codes also for 23- and 25-man squads (the original left stack leftovers in the slots from the 22nd on): the original 22 plus, in order, 0x202, 0x88 and 0x808, the slots the 24 table has beyond the 22 table. \n Ret 0x14, about 4.9 KB; SEH frame only for the local dates, no destructor: `NationalTeams::select_squad(nation, type, date, fixture, forced)`, from the call-up (0x76bab0, in Rust: nation +0x53 of the side, type, 0xae2c90, fixture, 0), from building the tables (0x76a840: fixture 0) and from the news (0x784100: forced 1). Type 0 senior, 1 B/Olympic (flag 8, tactic team 1), 2 under-21 (0x53b4f0). Without `forced`: in the final stages (+0x14 of the fixture in one of the 9 keys) an item (team, competition, match date − 10, 1000) goes into the list at +0 (0x68d0d0, created with 0x68d020 if missing); the squad date for the type (+0x3a of the record: today − 1 without a fixture, the match date in type 0 and above 2, the match date − 1 in types 1 and 2, which first mark both nations in vector `[this + 0x36]` at the Olympic Games or release the flagged under-21 player, 0x76d880) and today's (+0x32); the ages and the size (0x76d430 into +0x42/+0x43). With a human manager who decides (0x600a50, 0x5fd6b0; or through the main national side for a B team without a manager): players injured for more than 10 days (0x62c400 = 2, 0x62ed70 +0x2e) leave the squad; if it is still his, the request to the manager (0x76f1a0) and stop. Otherwise: the slot codes (squad_position_codes, with the 23 and 25 fix); those from another team leave the squad, those with the flag and, in type 0 with bit 1 of +0x4e of the fixture, those without it (0x896c60 and +0x5e/+0x24/+0x28); the pool list (collect_squad_candidates) goes to the slot assignment (0x6e2000, mode 0x2100914 in type 1, 0x2000814 in 0 and 0x814 in 2); each picked player who fits the slot (0x5b7d20) joins the squad: he leaves the previous team (slot, 0x76db00, 0x896c60) or his own tactic slots (0x8968f0/0x896e90, 0x76db00), gets the flag (0x540980), the team and +0x28 (0xc from 5 or 0xc, otherwise 0xb) and +9 of the 79-byte record goes to 0..100. Finally the squad is sorted (0x945333 with 0x778ef0), the news (0x76e0b0) and the tactic slots with those not in the team are cleared. The error boxes (lines 0x748 and 0x76b) as the original.

Returns the national side holding the player from the day before to the day after (a national side fixture in the window, against the given opponent if any, or a call-up already started) or the MLS all-star squad on the game date; writes the comment; otherwise 0 (and 0 for a national side or all-star club). \n Ret 0x14: `NationalTeams::get_international_duty_club(player, date, club, comment, opponent)`, from the line-up (0x6dbb80, 0x6dbc50), the scouts, the transfers and the screens. With a temporary list (0x68d020, destroyed at the end by 0x68d040). Club is a national side (0x53b900) or one of the all-star teams (id in `[0x9d00a4]`/`[0x9d00a8]`): 0. The window goes from the day before (0x54c8e0) to the day after (0x54c5b0). Called-up player (+0x24, the national side): the national side's matches in the window (0x5acbe0, side by bit 4 of +0x5e: set 1, otherwise 0; the days and years as the original's dwords); with a match and no opponent, or with the opponent (+0x14 of the match) among them, he is on duty (text 0xa62ff4 into `comment`, 0x66f4e0) and returns the national side. With bit 4 set, the call-ups of list `[this]` (+0 the national side, +4 the opponent, +8 the date) with his national side (and the opponent, if given) and a date before the requested one: he is in the team (text 0xa62fc8) and returns the national side. Otherwise the all-star team (competition `[[0xadadfc] + 4·[0x9cf690]]`: the match date through record +0xa3, day +3 and year +5 + year +0x40, 0x549ef0) for a club player (+0x39) of league `[0x9cf590]` (+0x57), with the date in the window: the 50 names (+0xd7) of both teams (first `[0x9d00a8]`; text 0xa62fa4 into 0xde1f64 if there is a `comment`). Otherwise 0.

Tells whether the player may play for the manager's national side: nationality, under-21 age, current call-up and the second-nationality rule. \n Stdcall, ret 8: `national_teams_player_is_eligible(player, manager)`, from the player search (0x7afa70, 0x807450) and from the comparison screen. No player sheet (+0x61), no national side for the manager (+0x24) or it not being a national side (0x53b900): 0. Already called up for it: 1. A national side of the second set (0x5409b0, the under-21) and age (+0x18) above 21: 0. With +0x22 or bit 2 of +0xc of the person's 79-byte record (`[0xae2d0c]`), the nationality (+0x1a) must be that of the national side (+0x53); called up for another national side of another nation: 0. The national side's nation must be the first or the second (+0x1e) nationality; if the nation is `[0x9cf434]` and so is the second: 0. Otherwise 1.

Adds to a list each duty competition it does not yet hold and returns how many were added. \n Ret 4: `NationalTeams::collect_duty_competitions(out)`, from the scouts (0x7f7010). Without the call-up list `[this]` or without `out`: 0. For each call-up, its competition (+4) goes into `out` (0x68d0d0, 4 bytes) if it is not there yet; returns how many were added (byte).

Selects the squads for a fixture: from two weeks before the match, for each side, a senior, B/Olympic or under-21 squad at most 14 days old and flagged only moves its date up to the match; otherwise asks for a new one (0x76c120); releases the over-age under-21 players and clears duplicates. \n Ret 4; SEH frame without a destructor: `NationalTeams::select_squads_for_fixture(fixture)`: without flag +0x40 with bit 1 of +0x4e, or with a B national side at home (0x5409b0) with bit 2, nothing. Only from two weeks before the match (0x54cab0 over date +0x2a/+0x28). Home side: outside a B national side, the senior squad (refresh_or_select_squad type 0) and, without bit 2, the release of the under-21 players (0x76d880) of both nations; the smaller squads (refresh_minor_squads). Away side: the same without the release. Finally deletes the duplicates (0x76c060) of both.

With a human manager at the player's club, sends news item 0x21 (the player, the national side and the slot) to the manager of club +0x39 and of the contract club. \n Stdcall, ret 0xc; SEH frame without a destructor: `national_teams_post_player_called_up_news(player, nation, slot)`: only with a human manager (0x7875e0) at the player's club +0x39 or at the contract club (which must exist). News 0x21 (local): 0 the id, 1..3 the +0x33 of +4, +8, +0xc; slot 0: 4 the senior national side (0x53b3d0), 5 = 0; slot 1: the senior side and 1; other: the B team (0x53b4f0) and 0. Delivered to the manager (0x7861e0) of +0x39, if any, and to that of the contract club when it is another one.

Records a result between two national sides: counts each nation's match; by competition, marks the general record, swaps the nationality or, in real internationals, scores the FIFA ranking and adds caps and goals to everyone who played; clears the type's +0x44 on its date and sends the news to the clubs. \n Ret 8: `NationalTeams::record_international_result(fixture, summary)`: only between two national sides (0x53b900). By the fixture's competition (`[+0x14]`): that of `[0x9cf794]` marks +0xd = 1 in the general record of those who played; that of `[0x9cf798]` sets bit 2 of +0xc and swaps the nation (+0x1a/+0x1e); that of `[0x9cf7a0]` nothing; the others: the FIFA ranking (0x58cf70 on `[this+0x1c]`) and, for those who played, the first call-up (0x86cc50 with the opponent, if +0x22 = 0, after the nation swap), a cap (+0x22) and the goals (+0x23 += +0x21 of the slot) for the national side and the match in the record (0x8ce920 with the nation's number of matches). In all of them, the nation's match count (+2) goes up. Then, per side: the type (1 if +0x40 = 0; otherwise 2 for the second team 0x5409b0, otherwise 0); on the type's date (+0x3a + 20 × type, 0x4a7f20 with today's) zeroes +0x44 + 20 × type; the news to the clubs (0x7706c0) with the star player (slot +0x153) and the list of those who played. No SEH, no box, no random draw.

Writes the squad name (Main, B, Under 21 or Under 23), in lower case when asked. \n Ret 0x14; `this` is not read: `NationalTeams::format_squad_label(type, under23, out, size, lowercase)`: size below 20: the box (line 0x1c98). Writes (0x66f4e0) the squad name: type 0 "Main", 1 "'B'", others "Under 23" (with under23) or "Under 21"; with lowercase = 1, in lower case.

Withdraws an injured player: with 14 or more injury days, removes the call-up from the national tactics and squad; before the squad date, tells his club, opens the slot and calls up a replacement or asks the human manager. \n Ret 8: `NationalTeams::withdraw_injured_player(p, days)`: with 14 or more days of injury, the called-up player (+0x28 = 0xb) of the national side's club (+0x24) leaves: with an injury of type 0x51 he only leaves the tactic (0x896c60, twice) and the squad (0x7762f0). Otherwise, only before the type's date (+0x3a of the type record: `[this+4]` + 0x6e × nation id + 20 × type; 0x456740 over `[0xae2c90]`) and if list `[this]` does not have the club with a date already past: the news to his club (0x76f7d0), the removal, the type's open slots (+0x45) go up 1, the level (0x76d810) and, if the national side's manager is human and decides (0x600a50, 0x5fd6b0), the request for a replacement (0x7701f0); otherwise the replacement (0x775f90) and the repeated call-ups deleted (0x76c060). Without a club: the original routine (box and 0).

Builds news item 0x20 (the player left the national squad injured) and delivers it to his club and his contract club when human-managed. \n Ret 0xc; SEH frame without a destructor; `this` is not read: `national_teams_post_player_withdrawn_news(p, nation, type)`: if the player's club (+0x39) or the contract club (0x4cf5a0) has a human manager (0x7875e0), builds news 0x20 in a local (0x77bbe0 with 0): data 0..3 the player and those of +4/+8/+0xc, 4 the national side's id (senior 0x53b3d0 in types 0 and 1, otherwise 0x53b4f0), 5 = (type == 1), 6 the injury severity; delivers it to club +0x39 and, if it is another one, to the contract club (0x7861e0).

Builds news item 0x22 (a replacement is needed) with the team, squad count, level and type, and delivers it to the national side's human manager. \n Ret 0x10; SEH frame without a destructor; `this` is not read: `national_teams_post_replacement_needed_news(p, nation, type, level)`: news 0x22 to the national side's manager: data 0..3 the player, 4 the team id (type 1: senior with flag 8 and 5 = 1; type 0: senior, otherwise the under-21 0x53b4f0, flag 4 and 5 = 0), 6 the injury severity, 7 = 0, 8 those in the squad with the flag (0x53c590), 9 the level, 0xa the type and 0xb the nation id. Delivered to the team if its manager is human (0x600a50), otherwise to the senior side if its manager is.

Tells whether the player may join or leave the squad now (retired, other nation, full squad, injured, squad window, date and match day, human manager) and writes the reason. \n Ret 0x18; SEH frame with the local list of the match search: `national_teams_can_change_squad(nation, type, p, joining, msg, size)`: a player (if any) retired from the national side (0x547d30) or from a club of another nation cannot change (0). The team of the type (0 and 1 the senior side, type 1 with flag 8 and the second team; otherwise the under-21 0x53b4f0, flag 4). Joining: a full squad (0x53c590 against +0x42 of the type record) or an injured player (0x62c400 = 2) cannot change. Can change (1): joining with open slots (+0x45), the type with no window (+0x44 = 0), the type's date (+0x3a) already past or, on the day itself, a team match today (0x5acee0 into a local list); in types 1 and 2 with a human manager who decides (0x600a50), also when list `[this]` does not have the team with a past date and he does not allow it (0x5fd6b0). The reasons go to `msg` (0x66f4e0). Without a nation, or `msg` with fewer than 0x32 bytes: the original routine (box and 1).

Tells whether the player is in the squad of the type (senior, second or under-21) with the type's flag. \n Stdcall, ret 0xc: `national_teams_player_in_squad(p, nation, type)`: 1 if the club of the player's national side (+0x24) is the team of the type (0 and 1 the senior side 0x53b3d0, 2 the under-21 0x53b4f0) and he has the type's flag (+0x5e: 4 in types 0 and 2, 8 in 1). No club or another type: 0.

qsort comparer of records by the date at +0 (0x456770/0x456740), earliest first. \n `compare_call_up_records_by_date(a, b)`: the qsort of records with the date at +0 (the 9-byte call-ups, the injuries, the transfers): −1 if that of `a` is earlier (0x456770), 1 if later (0x456740), otherwise 0. Hot (qsort): no counter.

With nation and finals both non-null, appends the pair to the new qualifiers list (+0x28). \n Ret 8: `NationalTeams::add_qualified_nation(nation, finals)`: with both non-null, appends the 8-byte record (nation, finals) to the list of new qualifiers at this + 0x28 (LLIST, 0x68d0d0).

In the call-up record list, those of the competition (+4) end tomorrow (+0x10, the day from 0x54c5b0). \n Ret 4: `end_duty_for_competition(comp)`: in the call-up record list `[this]`, those of the competition (+4 equal to *comp) end tomorrow (+0x10). No SEH, no box, no random draw; the local is the date that 0x54c5b0 writes.

In each club record (+0x20, 6 bytes), drops the expired entries (0x456770) at the start, moves the rest down (0x777590) and frees the emptied buffer. \n `prune_club_call_up_records()`: each club record (+0x20, 6 bytes: +0 vector of 9-byte entries, +4 flag, +5 count, signed byte) counts the entries already expired (0x456770: their date before `[0xae2c90]`; the routine assumes they are at the start), moves the others down over them (0x777590) and decreases the count; zeroed with a vector, frees the vector (0x9452ca) and zeroes +4 and +0. No SEH, no box, no random draw; the local (the expired count) is zeroed before being read.

Removes the person from the team tactics (0x896c60) and, if found in a slot, empties it and clears +0x24, +0x28 and the national bits of +0x5e. \n Ret 0xc: `remove_player_from_squad(nation, type, p)`: takes `p` out of the team's tactic (0x896c60, twice) and, if he is in one of the 50 slots (+0xd7), empties the slot and clears the person (+0x24, +0x28, +0x5e & 3). No SEH, no random draw, no locals; a box only with a null team or person (0x896c60).

Once the nation record date (+0x62) has passed, removes from the under-21 squad everyone older than 21 (+0x18) and clears record +0x6b. \n Ret 4: `release_overage_u21_players(nation)`: after the date of the nation record (+0x62/+0x66; 0x456740 over `[0xae2c90]`), each of the 50 slots of the under-21 side (0x53b4f0) with a person aged (+0x18, signed byte) above 21 leaves the tactic (0x896c60, twice), is cleared (+0x24, +0x28, +0x5e & 3) and the slot is emptied; finally zeroes byte +0x6b of the record. No SEH, no random draw; the local is `this`.

The nation's current competition (record +4) becomes −1 and, if there is a next one (`[this+8][id]`), that one takes its place, notifying the managers (0x6a3770). \n Ret 4: `clear_current_competition(nation)`: the current competition of the nation record (`[this+4]` + 0x6e × id, +4) becomes −1; if there is a next one (`[this+8][id]` ≠ −1), it becomes the current one, the next becomes −1 and the manager manager is notified (0x6a3770). No SEH, no box, no locals.

Calls up a replacement: in the pool of the level, the first eligible player of the nation who plays a position of the one leaving (0x5b7d20) is called up (0x776250, leaving another squad first through 0x7762f0) with the news (0x76fd10); nobody: clears the type's slot count (+0x45). \n Ret 0x10: `call_up_replacement(nation, type, level, leaving)`: in the section of the level (0x76d810) in the type's pool (`[this+0xc]`, under-21 `[this+0x10]`; start +8/+0x1d of the record plus the slots of the previous levels, count +0xd/+0x22), the first one who is not `leaving`, has a player sheet (+0x61), likes the club (0x547d30), is fit (0x62c400), is not a flagged regen (0x7a7eb0) outside the senior side, is from the nation (team +0x24, nationalities +0x1a/+0x1e, +0x22, bit 2 of the 79-byte record), is not suspended (0x55d270) and plays one of the positions of `leaving` (0x5b7d20). Without a team he goes straight in; called up (+0x28 = 0xb) for another type (2 with 0x5409b0, otherwise bit 3 of +0x5e) only after the type's date (+0x3a; 0x456770) and, for type 0, if the club allows (0x600a50): he leaves there (0x7762f0). He joins (0x776250), the type's slot (+0x45) goes down 1 and the news goes out (0x76fd10). Nobody: zeroes +0x45. No SEH, no random draw; the local for the type of the other squad is written before being read (only the byte counts).

Builds the selection pools: clears the 4 levels of each nation record and puts every eligible person in the nation pool (and the under-21 one, up to 21 years and under 5 caps), also by the second nationality; full section: enters by rating, and sorts (qsort with 0x778ed0). \n `build_selection_pools()`: zeroes the counts (+0xd, +0x22) and puts 10000 in the lowest ratings (+0xf, +0x24) of the 4 levels of each nation record (`[this+4]`, 0x6e bytes); then each person (`[0xae23bc]`, 0x6e bytes) with a nation (+0x1a), a player sheet (+0x61), over 16 years old (+0x18), without a national side or already called up (+0x24, +0x28 = 0xb), in a player position (0x53b620 of +0x3d) and with a club (+0x39) joins the nation's pool (add_to_reserves) and, up to 21 years with fewer than 5 caps (+0x22), the under-21 one; and again by the second nationality (+0x1e: with no caps for the first, a different one and not `[0x9cf434]`). No SEH, no box, no random draw; the locals are written before being read (of the rating stored in 32 bits only the short counts).

Takes the player out of his level pool in the nation and out of the squad, clearing his national team fields. \n Ret 4: takes `player` out of the national side. With a nation (+0x1a) and a player sheet (+0x61): in the nation's 110-byte record in `[this+4]`, the level (0x76d810 with the record and 0); if the level's rating (word +0xf + level × 4) is lower than the player sheet's (+9), looks for the player in the level's section of list `[this+0xc]` (start = dword +8 + bytes +0xe of the previous levels, size in byte +0xd + level × 4): found, the last of the section goes into his slot and the size decreases. Then, if called up (+0x24): his slot among the 50 (+0xd7) is zeroed, +0x24 is zeroed and byte +0x5e keeps only bits 0..1.

Returns the player's level 1..3 for the national side by reputation and position ratings. \n Stdcall, ret 0xc: the level 1..3 of player `j` for the national side (0 with reputation `*rep` below 100, or 50 with `base`, or a goalkeeper rated 15): 1 for sweeper or central defender, 2 for defensive midfielder, midfielder or attacking midfielder (rating 15 in +0x10..+0x14 of the player sheet), otherwise 3. Returns only `al`.

Returns the age limits (23/23 in youth competitions, 24/22, 26/22). \n Stdcall, ret 0x10: the age limits (`*minimum`, `*maximum`) of a national side in competition `comp`: 23/23 in the Olympic and youth competitions (`[comp+0x14]` with an id among the 9 constants 0x9cf78c…0x9cf964); 24/22 with `type` 1 or above 2; otherwise 26/22. Null pointers: the original routine (error box).

Sorts the national squad by club and adds, on the match date, how many players each club gives up (the record that stops club fixtures near that date). \n Ret 0xc; SEH frame only for the state, the dates have no destructor: `NationalTeams::record_club_call_ups(team, b, fixture)`: sorts the team's squad (+0xd7, 50 slots) by club (qsort with 0x778ef0). With the fixture: its date (+0x2a, +0x28; a day earlier for the second team 0x5409b0 or with `b`); counts the consecutive called-up players of each club (+0x39), skipping the empty slots, the persons out of range (`[0xae2364]`) and those of another squad (+0x5e bit 3 without `b`, bit 2 with it), and when the club changes adds the previous club's count to its record (add_club_callups). The last club of the loop gets no record (as in the original).

Picks a random pundit: type 1 on Sunday becomes 7; local types (2, 4): the club's pundits; the others: of the type and nation (−1 any); up to 20, random(n) and the id, or −1. \n Ret 0xc; 0x1094-byte frame through 0x945610: `PunditList::pick_random_pundit(club, type, nation)`, from the press stories (0x72c1f0, 0x733a60) and from the news texts. Type 1 on Sunday (0x54a3f0 = 6) becomes 7. Types 2 and 4 (local): those of list `[this+4]` whose +0xcb is the id of `[[club+0x69]+0x38]` (none: −1); the others: those of list `[this]` of the type (+0xca) and the nation (+0xcf; −1 accepts any). Up to 20; none: −1; otherwise the id (word +0, signed) of one of them by random(n).

Returns the name (+2) and flag (+0xd3) of the pundit with the id, or the default outlet type name and flag 0. \n Ret 0x10: `PunditList::get_pundit_name(type, id, name, flag)`, from the news texts. Without `name`: flag 0. Id −1: the type's default name and flag 0. Otherwise the pundit with the id (word +0) in list `[this+4]` (types 2 and 4) or `[this]`: the name (+2, sprintf "%s" 0x944c9f) and the flag (+0xd3); without him, the default name and flag 0.

Fills the match record as seen by the club: date, fixture id, competition, venue, club, opponent and goals for and against (the extra-time score, if any). \n `fill_match_record_from_fixture(match, club, out)`, from the tactic statistics (0x896290, at the end of each match without a human) and from the records. Null match, club or output: the box (lines 0x29, 0x31, 0x39) and 0. Otherwise the date (+0, 0x417c10 of the Date(day +0x2a, year +0x28) from 0x549ef0), +8 the match id (+0), +0xc word +0x32, +0xe word +0x30, +0x10 the side (0x4afa80, cdecl(club, match)), +0x11 the club id, +0x1b dword +8 of the match; home side (+0x1c): +0x15 the match's +0x10 and the score (+0x19 for, +0x1a against) from the extra-time one (+0x47/+0x48) if it is not negative, otherwise the normal one (+0x43/+0x44); away side: +0x15 the +0xc and the score reversed. Returns 1.

Stores the three name ids (−1 when missing), the person's id and birth date in a compact reference. \n `fill_staff_name_ref(person, out)`, from the club and competition records, the suspension news, the award and the player search. Null person or output: the box (lines 0x80, 0x88) and 0. Otherwise +0, +4, +8 the name ids (+4, +8, +0xc of the person; −1 with no name), +0xc the person's id and +0x10 the birth date (+0x10, 0x417c10); returns 1.

Returns the result code of the record: 3 win, 2 score draw, 1 goalless draw, −3 defeat. \n `match_record_result_code(record)`, from the competition statistics (0x49f570, on each match). Null record: the box (line 0x25a) and 0. For (+0x19) > against (+0x1a), signed: 3; draw with goals: 2; goalless draw: 1; defeat: −3 (only the byte counts: the caller reads al).

Tells whether the match record is a win by a larger margin than the other one, or the same margin with more goals scored. \n `match_record_is_bigger_win(a, b)`, from the club records after each match (0x444930) and from the competition ones (0x49fb93): 1 if `a` is a win (goals +0x19 > +0x1a, signed bytes) by a larger margin than that of `b`, or equal with more goals scored. Null record: the original routine ("Error" box, 0).

Tells whether the match record is a defeat by a larger margin than the other one, or the same margin with more goals conceded. \n `match_record_is_bigger_defeat(a, b)`, from the club records after each match (0x444930): 1 if `a` is a defeat (+0x19 < +0x1a) by a larger margin than that of `b`, or equal with more goals conceded. Null record: the original routine ("Error" box, 0).

Builds the red card ban: the matches or days from the offence code (9 to 12) and the body's scale, today's date and the player; 0 when there is no ban. \n Ret 0xc: `RulingBody::make_points_ban(record, player, by_matches)`, from each country's bodies (rb_*.cpp, when processing a match's red card): the offence code (+0x2e with +0x2c = 0, +0x2f with +0x2c = 1; another type: 0) gives, through the body's scale (+6), the matches (by_matches ≠ 0; the days stay 0xffff) or the days (the matches stay 0xff) of the ban. In the record: +0 matches, +1 = 0, +2 days, +4 today's date (`[0xae2c90]`, 0x417c10), +0x10 = 3, +0x1c the player's id (+0), +0x6f = (+0x48 of the player == 0). Returns 1; with no ban, 0 without writing anything.

At the new season, releases bans 2 (or 4) years old, frees the entries without a ban, clears the bookings of the others and compacts the table. \n Ret 0: `RulingBody::start_new_season()`: for each occupied disciplinary entry (14 bytes in `[this+0xb]`, count +0x13; id −1 is a free slot): with a ban (+6, signed index into the 20-byte discipline table `[[0xae28f0]+4]`) 2 or more years old (4 if the body has neither +0x17 nor +0x1b; the ban year in +6 against today's `[0xae2c92]`), releases the ban (0x556d00) and frees the entry; without a ban, frees the entry; otherwise zeroes the bookings (+4, +5, +8 and the low 6 bits of +0xd). Freeing: the player's stored slot in the body (0x55cb60 through slot +4) with the same +5 gets −1 in +6; without it, writes the slot (0x55cb20, type +5, −1); the entry's id becomes −1. At the end compacts the entries (0x7e9050, in this batch).

Removes the free entries from the body's discipline table, fixes the stored index of each moved player and reallocates with 100 spare rows. \n Ret 0: `RulingBody::compact_entries()`: removes the free entries (id −1) from the 14-byte table `[this+0xb]`, bringing the occupied ones to the front; each one that moves fixes the player's stored index (0x55cb60 through slot +4: with the same +5, the new index in +6; without it, 0x55cb20 with type +5 and the index). Count +0x13 = n, capacity +0xf = n + 100 and reallocates (0x945667) with (n + 100) × 14 bytes; out of memory, the box (line 0x594) and continues.

The scout manager's daily update, on day slice 2: prunes the scouting requests (non-human club, player already at the club, older than a year, 3 reports, injured); a request older than 30 days becomes up to 3 reports from the manager's scouts covering the player's nation and leaves; then the reports, the request order and one search tick on every human manager list. \n Ret 0; SEH frame for the local list and the dates: `SCOUT_MANAGER::daily_update()`, from the day (only on slice 2 of the day, `[0xae2c88]`; otherwise 0). Prunes the scouting requests (+0x5c, count +0x64, 0x11 bytes; the removed one gets the last one), and the processed request becomes up to 3 reports from the scouts of the club's manager (of the 10 lists, 0x7f6cd0, the one that covers the player's nation, 0x7b7490): 0x7b62a0 with −1000, mode 1, and the record (0x67 bytes) goes into the local list if byte +0x66 ended ≥ 0. Then the reports (0x7f9890), the request order (0x945333 with 0x7fc270) and one search (0x7b3e20) on each of the 10 lists of the human managers (the last 16 persons with +0x5f = 1). Returns 1.

Copies the list records into an array, sorts it and sends one news item per run of the same player and club. \n Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::send_scout_reports(list)`, from the scouts' day (0x7f8750) and from the search (0x7f8c00). With the list not empty (+0 count): a vector of count × 0x67 (0x944e46; out of memory, the box at line 0x7dd) with copies of the records, sorted (0x945333 with 0x7fc2a0); each consecutive group of the same player (+0x2b) and the same club (+0x50) becomes a report news item (0x7f9a60 with the first one and how many). Frees the vector (0x9452ca). The list is left with its cursor at the start.

Sends the 0x138e news item with up to 3 records, the scout, the match and the player's strengths for the club, to the club's manager. \n Ret 8; SEH frame for the local news item: `SCOUT_MANAGER::send_scout_report_news(record, count)`, from the reports (0x7f9890). News 0x138e (0x77bbe0): count (up to 3), +0x66, the scout (0x7e5160 with +0x1f), +0x59, +0x5a, club +0x50, the match data (0x7e4de0), +0x5e, +0x62, +0x58, +0x54, from each of the records (+0x37 + 0x67 × k) +0xc, +0, +4, +8 and +0x26 + 8 × +0x25, 0x420e9 and the player's (+0x2b) strengths for the club (0x546ab0); goes to the club's manager (0x7861e0).

Tells whether the current search of the current human manager session has no club (+0x191 = −2). \n Ret 0: `SCOUT_MANAGER::current_search_has_no_club()`, from the search screens (0x482a9b). The session of the human manager whose turn it is (`[this + 0xc + 4 × index]`): the current search (the signed byte at +0 of the session) without a club (+0x191 = −2). No manager or no session: 0; index out of range: the box (line 0x454; the original) and 0.

Tells whether one of the 10 searches of the current human manager session is for the club. \n Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::is_club_in_session_searches(club)`, from the screens (0x482aaf, 0x483040, 0x7b34e1). Any of the 10 searches of the session of the human manager whose turn it is has the club (+0x191 = +0 of the club): 1. No manager or no session: 0; index out of range: the box (line 0x480; the original) and 0.

The scouts at the match: for each human manager, the 10 scouts in a randomly drawn order; one for the playing club starts the assignment, and each watches the match; at the end the reports go out. \n Ret 8; SEH frame for the local LLIST 0x68d020/0x68d040: `SCOUT_MANAGER::scout_match(fixture, result)`, from the closing of the day's match (0x6b5f00, Rust). For each of the last 16 person records (`[0xae23bc]`, 0x6e bytes, from the last backwards) with +0x5f = 1 (the human manager): in a zeroed vector of 10 marks (0x945501), the 10 scouts in a random order (0x90cfc0 of 10 until an unmarked one is found); each one's record (0x7f6cd0) with +0x19d, in a fixture with flags +0x40 and +0x41 and of the manager's club (+0x39 = +0x1c or +0x20 of the fixture), starts the scouting (0x7ae9c0 with −1, −1, −1, 0, 1); and watches the match (0x7b5be0, the reports into the local list). The vector is freed (0x9452ca). Finally the reports go out (0x7f9890) and the list is destroyed. Returns 1.

Returns the human manager's searches edit session. \n Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::get_edit_session(manager)`, from building the search's known players (0x7afeb7). The human manager's edit session (+0xc + 4 × index). No manager or index out of range: the box (lines 0xde and 0xe8; the original) and 0.

Stores the human manager's searches edit session and returns 1. \n Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::set_edit_session(session, manager)`, from the search screens (0x8085bc, 0x812d88...). Writes the session into +0xc + 4 × the manager's index and returns 1. No manager or index out of range: the box (lines 0xb8 and 0xc2; the original) and 0.

Returns the list selected by the human manager (null: the current one). \n Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::get_selected_list(manager)`, from the search screens (0x804248). The list chosen by the human manager (byte at +0x4c + index). No manager or outside 0..15: the original routine ("Error" box, 0xff).

Stores the list selected by the human manager (null: the current one). \n Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::set_selected_list(list, manager)`, from the search screens (0x804460). Writes the chosen list (byte) into +0x4c + the human manager's index and returns 1. No manager or outside 0..15: the original routine ("Error" box, 0).

Tells whether the fixture has a watched club or an available player with a scout request (at the club or national side, not loaned out, injured, suspended or barred, and not yet played). \n Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::fixture_has_scouted_player(fixture)` (from match_without_human 0x6b66a0): negative competition (+0), 0. A club of the watched list (static LLIST 0xb74438, cursor reset; +0 of the item) equal to +0xc or +0x10 of the fixture, 1. Then the scouting requests (`[this+0x5c]`, 0x11 bytes, the person at +4, count `[this+0x64]`, reread on each step): a person whose club (+0x39) or national side (+0x24) is one of the two in the fixture (+0x1c first, then +0x20), who is not loaned out (0x8c7560, outside a national side 0x53b900), nor injured (0x62c400 = 2), nor suspended (0x55d270), nor barred (0x7757d0), and who has not played yet (0x8cf5e0 = 0), gives 1. Otherwise 0.

Tells whether the player is on the human's scouting shortlist (through the open edit session or the first type 1 search). \n Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::is_player_shortlisted(person, manager)` (from the interested clubs 0x842180, from the status 0x849d60, from 0x8cde70 and from screens): null person, the "Error" box (line 0x231) and 0; without a manager, that of the human whose turn it is (without him, the box at line 0x23b and 0). The human's slot (byte +0 of the manager − byte of `[0xae2364]` + 16, signed, 0..15): with the edit session open (`[this + slot × 4 + 0xc]`), its answer (0x804540); otherwise the first of the 10 searches (0x7f6cd0) of type 1 (+0xa) answers (0x7af600). Without it, 0.

Returns the human manager's scouting record 0..9 (0x2b0 bytes). \n Ret 8: scouting record `which` 0..9 of human manager `manager` (without him, the one whose turn it is in `[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × [0xb77c7a]]`): the index (id − `[0xae2364]` + 16) × 10 + `which`, up to `[this+8]` − 1, with 0x2b0 bytes each starting at `[this]`. `which` out of range, no manager or index out of range: the original routine (error box).

Empties the list and adds the person of each scout request of the club; returns whether there is any. \n Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::collect_club_scout_targets(club, list)`: with `list`, empties it (0x68d080) and adds (0x68d0d0, 0x6e bytes) the person of each scouting request of club `*club`. Returns whether there is any. Null club: 0 (the list stays empty).

Removes a scout request: finds the request (club, person; 17 bytes), pulls the next ones up and sorts again (0x7fc270); null club = the current human manager's club. \n Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::remove_scout_request(person, club)`: a null club is that of the current human manager (`[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × [0xb77c7a]]`, +0x39; without him, nothing). With a rival, the slot joins the rival's list of offers for the player (+0, 0x68d0d0), or a new one with the rival and it. The deadline: with +0x2f, status 7 and 28 days if the buyer is human (0x600a50 with 0, 1, 0, 0), otherwise nothing; without +0x2f, 28 days if the seller (the club of the target's contract) is human, otherwise the reply deadline (0x8cc5b0), scheduled (0x8c6220) if it gives days or slices. The news: loan offered (0x8e1780 with the terms) or offer made (0x8d3090). The target's 8-byte record (`[this+0x86e]`): bit 0 of +0 and +1 goes up; +2 of each exchange player goes up. A human buyer and a target with a player sheet (+0x61): 0x7f75f0 (`[0xb74448]`, target, 0).

Screens only: the club accepts the loan request; the contract decision, the news, and without agreement status 0xf, the shortlists, the 10-day scheduling and bit 0 of the player record. \n Ret 8: `TRANSFER_MANAGER::accept_loan_offer(slot, mark)`, only from the transfer screen (0x8ef1e0) and the news (0x784100). The computer seller answers a bid: loan bids are refused without looking at anything else; unless a rule makes it accept, the floor fee and the other offers, the exchange value, the cash, exchange and clause options; an option worth less than the bid / 0.85 accepts, the best one under the bid / 0.75 becomes a counter offer, otherwise refuses.

The most attractive one is the best; the first whose value (0x8e7b50 with 0, 0, 1, 1, 1) × 0.85 is below the asking price, with no refused exchange: accepted (outside the dry run). No best: the box (line 0x1eee) and the refusal, without freeing the options.

Otherwise the buyer's squad (0x541f90 with 0: 50 slots), the new offer (0x944cf1 of 0x41 bytes and 0x8e5680) in *out, prepared (0x8e78f0: push value; push buyer; push target; mov ecx, offer), attraction 50, +0x1b = value and the ceiling = value × 1.1 (_ftol). Then the target himself and the 50 of the squad with the same position: a contract with the candidate's current club (0x4cf5f0) of a type other than 5, at the buyer, without a sheet (0x4cf6d0), without bits 0x30 of +0xb of the 79-byte record, floor (0x4d1600 with 0, 1, 1) up to the ceiling; with no offer (0x8c5cf0), exchange (0x8c5e40 in the local list) or exchange negotiation of the target (0x8c5fc0), or only this offer's exchange (+0x20); the seller can reach him (0x8ce990 with 0, 1); interest (0x846920: push 0; push status; push 0; push 1; push seller; push player; mov ecx, `[this+0x856]`) of at least 3.15; his rating / the base above 0.9: the attraction rises 20 (higher rating) or 5, between 0 and 100; not yet in the exchange (+4, created if missing), he joins it (0x68d0d0 with 7 bytes: id, 0, status), his value (0x840d80 with −1, 1) is taken off the ceiling and off +0x1b (at least 0), and the slot ends. Returns 1.

The seller accepts the bid: status 5; on loans, target interest below 0.75 gives the refusal to move; exchange players wanting more than 1.5 times the seller's wage cap leave, with their value added to the fee; the offer goes to the next slice.
